title: Dendrobine regulates STAT3 to attenuate mitochondrial dysfunction and senescence in vascular endothelial cells triggered by oxidized low-density lipoprotein.
authors: Xia, Jia; Chen, Jingyi; Xing, Xinyue; Meng, Jing; Song, Xiaoying; Lou, Danfei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物dendrobine通过STAT3/FoxO信号通路缓解内皮细胞线粒体功能障碍与衰老，虽涉及分子对接但核心为细胞表型与信号通路实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Our previous studies have highlighted the potential therapeutic efficacy of dendrobine, an alkaloid, in atherosclerosis (AS), nevertheless, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study employs a combination of network pharmacology and in vitro experiments to explore the regulatory pathways involved. Through network pharmacology, the biological function for intersection targets between dendrobine and AS were identified. Molecular docking was conducted to investigate the interaction between the dominant target and dendrobine. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were treated with oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) to mimic AS, and the effects of dendrobine on cell viability, lipid deposition, mitochondrial function, and cellular senescence were evaluated. Subsequently, cells were treated with the mitophagy inhibitor Mdivi-1 and the STAT3 agonist colivelin to assess the role of mitophagy and STAT3 signaling in dendrobine regulation. Intersection targets were associated with biological processes, including reactive oxygen species production. Dendrobine attenuated the effects of ox-LDL treatment on HUVECs, mitigating changes in cell activity, lipid deposition, mitochondrial function, and cellular senescence. Both Mdivi-1 and colivelin treatments resulted in decreased cell viability and increased cellular senescence, with colivelin suppressing mitophagy. Cotreatment with Mdivi-1 and colivelin further aggravated cellular senescence and inhibited FoxO signaling. Together, this study indicated that dendrobine regulated the STAT3/FoxO signaling pathway, alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence. This study contributes valuable insights to the potential clinical application of dendrobine.
abstract_zh: 我们前期的研究已凸显石斛碱（dendrobine），一种生物碱，在动脉粥样硬化（AS）中的潜在治疗功效，然而其潜在机制尚不明确。本研究结合网络药理学和体外实验，探讨其涉及的调控通路。通过网络药理学，我们鉴定了石斛碱与AS交集靶点的生物学功能。采用分子对接（molecular docking）研究主要靶点与石斛碱之间的相互作用。人脐静脉内皮细胞（HUVECs）经氧化低密度脂蛋白（ox-LDL）处理以模拟AS，并评估石斛碱对细胞活力、脂质沉积、线粒体功能和细胞衰老的影响。随后，用线粒体自噬抑制剂Mdivi-1和STAT3激动剂colivelin处理细胞，以评估线粒体自噬和STAT3信号在石斛碱调控中的作用。交集靶点与生物过程相关，包括活性氧产生。石斛碱减弱了ox-LDL对HUVECs的作用，缓解了细胞活性、脂质沉积、线粒体功能和细胞衰老的变化。Mdivi-1和colivelin处理均导致细胞活力下降和细胞衰老增加，其中colivelin抑制了线粒体自噬。Mdivi-1和colivelin联合处理进一步加剧了细胞衰老并抑制了FoxO信号。综上，本研究表明石斛碱调控STAT3/FoxO信号通路，缓解线粒体功能障碍和细胞衰老。本研究为石斛碱的潜在临床应用提供了有价值的见解。
